name: Tanzlinde (Effeltrich)
age_estimate: roughly 600-800 years, popularly called the "1000-year lime"

location.address: Village square (Dorfplatz) beside the Wehrkirche St. Georg, Effeltrich, Landkreis Forchheim

access: Free, public village square beside the fortified church.
transport: Not verified; no confirmed public transport stop found. Effeltrich lies in the Franconian Switzerland foothills near Forchheim/Erlangen, reachable by car; no rail station in the village itself.
verify_notes: Single-tree-destination exception (2026-08-31 ruling): a nationally recognised specimen, designated Nationalerbe-Baum (National Heritage Tree) No. 39 on 10 August 2024, one of a small national list. Two independent sources agree closely: baumkunde.de (girth 7.89m, measured 15 July 2025, height 8.0m) and nationalerbe-baeume.de (girth 8.02m, measured May 2024, height approx 8m); recorded the more recent baumkunde figure with the small disagreement flagged. Both give an age estimate of 600-800 years based on trunk structure and growth habit; the popular local name calls it the '1000-jaehrige Linde' (thousand-year lime), which is folklore repeated at the site and should be presented as a nickname, not a fact. Coordinates from the two sources agree to within a few metres, tree-level confirmed. Remarkable feature: the crown is a roughly 20m-wide flat disc trained horizontally over centuries onto an oak support structure of two concentric ring-beams on 24 posts, itself resting on a stone wall (49m long, 90cm high) that encircles the tree; pruned biennially to keep the form. Historic use as the village's Gerichts- und Tanzplatz (assembly, court and dance site); still hosts music and processions today. Alive and vital per baumkunde's most recent visit (15 July 2025). Genuinely a destination in its own right: sits on Franconia's tree-trail circuit and draws visitors specifically for the support structure, distinct from an ordinary village lime.
